questions.q:
A train travels at a constant speed of 54 km/h.
(a) Change 54 km/h into metres per second. [1]
(b) How many seconds does the train take to travel 600 m? [1]
questions.tip: km/h → m/s: multiply by 1000 and divide by 3600 (or divide by 3.6).

ms: B1: any two of the three terms 20x³, −6x, +2 correct
B1: 20x³ − 6x + 2 fully correct with no constant term
questions.tip: The constant −7 differentiates to 0, and 2x differentiates to 2.

questions.q:
A bus starts from rest and accelerates uniformly for 15 seconds until its speed is 12 m/s.
It then travels at 12 m/s for 40 seconds.
It then decelerates uniformly to rest in 10 seconds.
(a) Calculate the acceleration during the first 15 seconds. [1]
(b) Calculate the total distance travelled. [3]
(c) Calculate the average speed for the whole journey. [1]
ms: (b) M1: one correct area, e.g. ½ × 15 × 12 = 90
(b) M1: complete method for total area, e.g. 90 + 40 × 12 + ½ × 10 × 12 or ½(40 + 65) × 12
questions.model:
(a) 12 ÷ 15 = 0.8 m/s².
(b) Area under the speed–time graph:
½ × 15 × 12 + 40 × 12 + ½ × 10 × 12 = 90 + 480 + 60 = 630 m.
(c) Total time 15 + 40 + 10 = 65 s. Average speed = 630 ÷ 65 = 9.69 m/s.
questions.tip: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time, not the mean of the speeds.

questions.q:
A curve has equation y = x³ − 2x² + 5.
(a) Find the gradient of the curve at the point (2, 5). [2]
(b) Find the x-coordinate of the other point on the curve where the gradient is the same as at (2, 5). [2]
ms: (b) M1: 3x² − 4x = 4 and attempt to solve, e.g. (3x + 2)(x − 2) = 0
questions.model:
(a) dy/dx = 3x² − 4x. At x = 2: 12 − 8 = 4.
(b) 3x² − 4x = 4 → 3x² − 4x − 4 = 0 → (3x + 2)(x − 2) = 0.
x = 2 is the given point, so the other point has x = −2/3.
questions.tip: The gradient is dy/dx, not y: substitute into the derivative.

questions.q:
A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to a speed of V m/s in 20 seconds.
It travels at V m/s for 60 seconds, then decelerates uniformly to rest in 15 seconds.
The total distance travelled is 1395 m.
(a) Find V. [3]
(b) Calculate the deceleration. [1]
(c) Find the speed of the car 85 seconds after it started. [2]
ms: (a) M1: area expression, e.g. ½ × 20V + 60V + ½ × 15V or ½(60 + 95)V
(c) M1: recognises the car has been decelerating for 5 s: 18 − 5 × 1.2 oe
questions.model:
(a) Distance = ½ × 20 × V + 60V + ½ × 15 × V = 10V + 60V + 7.5V = 77.5V.
77.5V = 1395 → V = 18.
(b) Deceleration = 18 ÷ 15 = 1.2 m/s².
(c) Deceleration starts at t = 80 s, so at t = 85 s it has slowed for 5 s.
Speed = 18 − 5 × 1.2 = 12 m/s.
questions.tip: Sketch the speed–time graph and label the times; the area gives one equation in V.

questions.q:
A curve has equation y = 2x³ + 3x² − 36x + 10.
(a) Find dy/dx. [2]
(b) Find the coordinates of the two turning points. [4]
(c) Determine whether each turning point is a maximum or a minimum. Show how you decide. [2]
ms: (c) M1: d²y/dx² = 12x + 6 evaluated at both points, or sign of dy/dx either side, or reference to the shape of a positive cubic
questions.tip: Substitute into the original equation for y, not into dy/dx.
